sanskrit_verse: datto 'paviddhaḥ krītaś ca kṛtaḥ śaudras tathaiva ca / jātiśuddhā madhyamās te sarve rikthasutāḥ smṛtāḥ // BrhS_1,26.72
transliteration: dattaḥ apaviddhaḥ kṛtaś ca kṛtaḥ śaudraḥ tathaiva ca / jātiśuddhā madhyamās te sarve rikthasutāḥ smṛtāḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: Those born of purchased, abandoned, made, done, cleansed, or intermediate women—these are all declared as sons of the sacrificial fee.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from sacramental completion, not biological lineage alone
Causation arises through ritual integrity, not social presumption
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by spiritual eligibility, not birth status
Restoration logic prioritizes ontological inclusion over genealogical exclusion
Consciousness alignment supersedes caste-position in determining rightful participation
executable_legal_axioms: IF a child's origin involves transactional or non-ritually pure conception, THEN classify under 'rikthasuta' framework
IF classified as rikthasuta, THEN eligibility for rights derives from purification completion, NOT hereditary claim
IF societal function requires capacity verification, THEN initiate consciousness-readiness assessment prior to role assignment
IF exclusionary bias arises due to natal category, THEN enforce restorative integration via dharma-adhikara recognition process
IF dispute emerges concerning inheritance or duty, THEN resolve according to presence of diksha-bindu and atma-sambandha
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that legal personhood and functional eligibility must be evaluated based on completed diksha and consciousness-readiness rather than inherited caste identity. The threshold of responsibility lies in alignment with dharma-vakya, not familial genealogy.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that cause-effect relations in dharmic law stem from samskara completeness, not punitive attribution. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential unfoldment of purified identity regardless of natal condition. Responsibility aligns proportionally with awakened capacity. Reality remains non-punitive when judgment flows from vidyā-sattā rather than karmic debt enforcement.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Svayambhu Diksha Process to establish purified identity
Assign Atma-Vidya Mentorship to restore full consciousness access
Complete Riktha-Homa to dissolve residual karmic-social imprints
Reintegrate into varna-dharma through Shaktipat-based qualification assessment
Declare Antahkarana Samarthanam as sole basis for future entitlements
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as sourced from His Avataric Intelligence. Dharma is restored. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
